title: My Mom Said My Games Were Heating Up Our Whole House #shorts

cast.mom: a stick-figure mother with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, a curly red hair bun and a green sweater
cast.girl: a stick-figure girl with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, two black pigtails and a purple hoodie

lines.text: Mom said my gaming was heating up our house, so what was really heating it?
lines.label: hook
lines.headline: who heated the house
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, standing in a living room fanning herself with one hand next to exactly one small game console, worried face, afternoon

lines.text: All month, our air conditioner ran nonstop every afternoon, and the power bill kept climbing.
lines.label: setup
lines.headline: ac runs nonstop
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, standing in a kitchen holding up exactly one paper bill, shocked face, mouth open, afternoon

lines.text: Mom said, "Your console blows hot air all afternoon, right when the house gets hottest."
lines.label: the charge
lines.headline: mom blames console
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, standing in a living room with arms crossed, pointing at exactly one small flat black game console box with one controller lying beside it on a low shelf, no TV in the picture, stern face, mouth open talking

lines.text: She locked my console in the hall closet, right beside her shiny new birthday mirror.
lines.label: stakes
lines.headline: console locked away
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, putting exactly one small game console into a hallway closet, a big round wall mirror hanging on the hallway wall beside the closet, stern face

lines.text: But the next afternoon, with my console unplugged, the air conditioner roared on anyway.
lines.label: worse
lines.headline: ac still runs
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, standing in a living room beside an empty shelf, looking up at an air vent on the ceiling, eyes wide, afternoon

lines.text: Mom said I must be sneaking the closet key, so she took my tablet too.
lines.label: more blame
lines.headline: tablet gone too
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, standing in a hallway holding exactly one tablet up high out of reach, frowning, evening light

lines.text: I sat shivering in my hoodie and cried, blamed for heat I never even made.
lines.label: alone
lines.headline: blamed and cold
lines.image: close-up of {girl} sitting alone on her bed hugging her knees, shivering, a single tear running down her cheek, sad eyes looking down, dim bedroom

lines.text: Then I noticed the cold blasts only started at three, and only on sunny days.
lines.label: the pattern
lines.headline: only at three
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, standing by a window with bright sunshine pouring in, cold air from a ceiling vent blowing her pigtails, finger raised, realizing face, afternoon

lines.text: In games, every timed monster has a trigger, so at three I watched the thermostat.
lines.label: gamer clue
lines.headline: every spawn has a trigger
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, sitting cross-legged on her bedroom floor, thinking hard with one finger on her chin, a simple drawing of a cartoon monster next to an hourglass in a thought bubble above her head

lines.text: Sunlight through the window hit Mom's mirror and bounced a beam onto the hallway thermostat.
lines.label: the twist
lines.headline: the mirror beam
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, peeking around a hallway corner, sunlight streaming through a window hits a big round wall mirror and bounces one bright beam of light onto exactly one small white wall thermostat with a round dial, eyes wide, afternoon

lines.text: Baking in that beam, it read eighty-five in a freezing house, so it kept cooling.
lines.label: the proof
lines.headline: fooled by the sun
lines.image: close-up of {girl} in her purple hoodie touching exactly one small white wall thermostat with a round dial that glows in a bright patch of sunlight on the hallway wall, surprised face, no numbers or text

lines.text: Mom moved her mirror and returned my console, but swears it still heats my room.
lines.label: the ending
lines.headline: console back
lines.image: {mom} is the only person in the picture, walking down a hallway carrying exactly one big round mirror in both hands in front of her, the only mirror in the picture, rolling her eyes, grumpy smile, late afternoon
